title: Impact of AI Search Summaries on Website Traffic
content:
Computer Science > Computers and Society
  [Submitted on 5 Feb 2026 (v1), last revised 2 Sep 2026 (this version, v6)]
Title:Impact of AI Search Summaries on Website Traffic: Evidence from Google AI Overviews and Wikipedia
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:Search engines increasingly display AI-generated answers above organic links, potentially displacing traffic to upstream publishers. We estimate the impact of Google's AI Overviews (AIO) on Wikipedia's search traffic using AIO's staggered geographic rollout and Wikipedia's multilingual structure. Our difference-in-differences design compares monthly external-search referrals to English Wikipedia articles with referrals to the same articles in German and French, and finds that default AIO availability reduced English search traffic by 5.45% and 4.82%, respectively. Our results suggest that answer-producing digital intermediaries can materially reallocate attention away from informational publishers, with implications for content monetization, search platform design, and policy.

report.summary: A difference-in-differences study using Google AI Overviews' staggered geographic rollout finds AI-generated answers cut search referrals to English Wikipedia by roughly 5%.
report.background: Search engines have been adding AI-generated answer boxes above traditional blue links since Google began rolling out AI Overviews in 2024. This has triggered a long-running fight over the economics of the open web: publishers supply the source material, but the click that funds them may never happen. Wikipedia is the ideal test case because the same articles exist across dozens of language editions, letting researchers compare traffic where AI Overviews were switched on by default against nearly identical content in markets where they were not. Earlier evidence on the 'zero-click' web was largely anecdotal or vendor-reported; this paper offers a quasi-experimental estimate. The finding lands as regulators, news organizations, and AI licensing negotiations all hinge on exactly how much attention is being diverted upstream.
key_points: The paper exploits a natural experiment: Google's AI Overviews arrived in different countries at different times. The researchers compare monthly external-search referrals to English Wikipedia against the same articles in German and French, where the feature rolled out on a different schedule.

Using a difference-in-differences design, the authors estimate that default AI Overview availability reduced English Wikipedia's search traffic by 5.45% relative to German and 4.82% relative to French. The two comparisons give a consistent magnitude.

The key phrase is 'default availability' — the effect reflects the feature being on for ordinary users by default, not a one-off experiment where people opted in. That mirrors how most people actually experience search today.

The authors argue answer-producing intermediaries can 'materially reallocate attention away from informational publishers.' Because Wikipedia is non-commercial and highly ranked, the hit to commercial publishers that earn ad revenue is plausibly larger in relative terms.
The study focuses on one large destination and one search engine, so the numbers are best read as a lower-bound directional signal rather than a universal estimate for the whole web.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is hard evidence undercutting the comfortable claim that AI answers expand the audience for content. If a top-ranked, universally recognized source like Wikipedia loses roughly 5% of search referrals, the value proposition of AI licensing deals shifts — publishers now have a measurable bargaining chip when negotiating compensation. For developers, it means retrieval-augmented and citation-centric designs should surface sources visibly and give users a reason to click, since AI-answer traffic does not come back. For regular users, the practical effect is subtle but real: free information ecosystems are funded by attention, and less of it flowing upstream can mean fewer independent sources, thinner updates, and more content locked behind paywalls or sponsorship.
report.tools: Readers can follow up with alphaXiv for community discussion of this preprint, Connected Papers and Litmaps to map the surrounding citation network, and Hugging Face or CatalyzeX to find linked code and data. For independent measurement, Wikimedia's Pageviews and Analytics APIs let you track real referral trends, while Google Search Console, Similarweb, and Common Crawl can corroborate traffic and crawl shifts. Google Trends is useful as a coarse cross-language control.
